To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have prepared a flexible glucose sensor based on Au dimpled titanium heterostructures modified by Nafion membrane, which is able to detect low concentrations of glucose in the range of 30 1000 mM with high sensitivity, selectivity and repeability.
the Au Ti heterostructure with 10 nm gold layer, covered with Nafion membrane is a promising material for the fabrication of flexible, biocompatible glucose sensor.
we have developed flexible, fully biologically compatible electrode material based on gold nanoparticles immobilized onto Ti dimples.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of flexible glucose sensor based on Au nanoparticles on dimpled titanium substrate.

the design, fabrication and characterization of flexible and highly biocompatible electrode materials based on Au nanoparticles deposited onto titanium dimples and modified by permselectivemembrane Nafion for glucose sensing applications.
the design of flexible and fully biocompatible electrodes based on gold nanoparticles immobilized onto Ti dimples.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have successfully developed a flexible, biocompatible, and selective glucose sensor, which could potentially be used in a non-invasive manner.
the presented material is a promising candidate for the noninvasive glucose sensing.
this study has shown the potential of Au Ti heterostructured electrode material as a basis for the development of a flexible glucose sensor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have prepared an enzyme free, flexible glucose sensor based on gold dewetted Ti structures.

we have demonstrated that it is possible to use the Nafion coated Au dimpled Ti electrode as a glucose sensor with a limit of detection of about 30 mM and with a high sensitivity of about 93 mAcm-2mM-1.
we have demonstrated the possibility of fabricating flexible, fully biodegradable glucose sensor based on Nafion coated Au nanoparticles immobilized on Ti dimples.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the developed electrode material can be used for glucose detection in human biofluids.
we were able to fabricate flexible, fully biodegradable electrode based on Nafion and Au nanoparticles immobilized on titanium dimples.
the combination of Au Ti heterostructure and Nafion membrane is an excellent material for the development of glucose sensor for the detection of glucose in noninvasive human biofluids.
